title_zh: Los Altos、Mountain View 与 Palo Alto 看房：收纳空间够不够，怎样判断？
title_en: Touring Homes in Los Altos, Mountain View, or Palo Alto: Will the Storage Work for You?
summary_zh: 柜子数量只是起点。从每天带进家门的物品，到工作设备与周末用品，用一份家庭清单观察收纳位置、尺寸和使用动线。
summary_en: Closet count is a starting point. Use a household inventory to assess storage locations, dimensions, and access—from everyday bags to work equipment and weekend gear.
body_zh:
看房时，整齐的衣柜和空旷的车库容易让人觉得“收纳应该够用”。更具体的判断方法，是把自己家真实使用的物品带进想象里：东西放在哪里，谁来取，用完怎样收回去？

在 Los Altos、Mountain View 或 Palo Alto 比较房屋时，可以给收纳留出一次专门观察的时间。

一、先列日常用品，再看柜子
把物品分成每天使用、每周使用和偶尔使用三组。例如通勤包、孩子的书包、工作设备、运动用品和旅行箱。每组挑出几件最占地方、最难安排的物品，记录尺寸和使用者。

这份清单不用精确到每件小物品。它的作用，是提醒你观察家庭生活真正需要的位置。

二、沿着回家路线走一遍
想象从常用入口进门：鞋、外套、钥匙和包会放在哪里？拿完物品后，家人是否还容易通行？再走到厨房、工作区和卧室，看看用品能否靠近使用地点收纳。

一个很大的柜子，如果离使用位置很远，也可能需要家人每天多走几趟。把这种体验写在看房笔记里，比只记录柜子数量更有帮助。

三、量清楚可用空间
经允许后，量一下关键柜体的内部尺寸、门口宽度和搁板之间的高度。留意柜门是否能充分打开，拿取较大物品是否方便。对特别在意的尺寸，安排后续核实；不要仅凭照片或目测决定购买收纳家具。

也要与经纪人确认哪些可移动柜体或架子属于卖方物品，以及交易中需要另行明确的事项。

四、把车库的多种用途一起考虑
如果你计划同时停车、存放自行车和收纳杂物，把这些用途放进同一张草图。用自己的车辆和物品尺寸核对，而不是假设照片里的空地都可用于收纳。固定设备周围需要保留多少空间，应请相应专业人员确认。

五、给不常使用但重要的物品留位置
季节用品、旅行箱与家庭备用物资，也需要有明确的存放位置。Ready.gov 的应急物资清单提醒家庭结合自身成员及宠物的特殊需求准备物资；可把这份官方清单作为整理家庭备用用品的参考。
官方参考：https://www.ready.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/ready_supply-kit-checklist.pdf

六、把“现有可用”和“以后想做”分开
现成的储物空间可以直接观察。定制柜、车库改造或其他更新计划，则需要进一步确认可行性、费用和时间。把它们分别记下，避免在比较房屋时把尚未落实的方案当作现有条件。

最后，可以为每套房写三句话：哪些物品已经有合适位置，哪些需要改变习惯，哪些仍需核实。收纳是否合适，取决于空间与你们生活方式的配合。

body_en:
A tidy closet or an empty garage can make a home look ready for everything you own. A more useful test is to picture the belongings your household actually uses: where would they go, who would retrieve them, and how would they be put away?

When comparing homes in Los Altos, Mountain View, or Palo Alto, set aside part of a tour specifically for storage.

1. Start with belongings rather than cabinets
Group items into daily, weekly, and occasional use. Think about work bags, school backpacks, office equipment, sports gear, and luggage. Identify a few bulky or difficult-to-store items in each group, along with their dimensions and users.

You do not need a complete household inventory. The purpose is to keep your real storage needs visible during the tour.

2. Follow the route home
Imagine entering through the door you would normally use. Where would shoes, coats, keys, and bags go? Could other household members still move through easily? Continue to the kitchen, workspace, and bedrooms, considering whether items could be stored near where they are used.

A large closet far from an activity may create extra trips every day. Record these observations alongside the number of cabinets and closets.

3. Check usable dimensions
With permission, measure key cabinet interiors, openings, and shelf spacing. Notice whether doors open fully and larger items could be retrieved comfortably. Arrange follow-up verification for important measurements before ordering storage furniture.

Ask your agent which freestanding cabinets or shelving belong to the seller and what needs to be clarified in the transaction.

4. Consider all the garage uses together
If you expect to park a car, keep bicycles, and store household items, put those uses on the same sketch. Work from your own vehicle and equipment dimensions rather than assuming every empty area in a photograph is available for storage. Ask an appropriate professional about required access or clearances around fixed equipment.

5. Make room for occasional but important items
Seasonal belongings, luggage, and household backup supplies need a defined home too. Ready.gov’s emergency supply checklist encourages households to consider the particular needs of family members and pets. It can serve as a reference when organizing those supplies.
Official reference:
https://www.ready.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/ready_supply-kit-checklist.pdf

6. Separate existing space from future ideas
You can observe the storage that exists today. Custom cabinetry, garage changes, or other improvements require further investigation of feasibility, cost, and timing. Keep those plans separate so an unresolved idea does not become an assumed feature when comparing properties.

After each tour, write three short notes: what already has a suitable place, what would require a change in habits, and what still needs verification. Useful storage depends on how the space fits your household.
